    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] VS Code extension file write within 120s of opening a .ipynb notebook (one-click install chain) · Suspicious browser extension installation
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] VS Code (code.exe) outbound network egress to non-Microsoft/non-GitHub domain
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Mass GitHub private repository enumeration in short window (stolen OAuth token reuse) · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
[LLM] VS Code (code.exe) outbound network egress to non-Microsoft/non-GitHub domain Command & Control Medium
Hunts for code.exe making HTTP/HTTPS connections to destinations outside the expected Microsoft + GitHub + extension marketplace footprint. Catches the OAuth-token exfiltration leg of Askar's github.dev webview exploit, where a malicious VS Code extension installed via the .ipynb onerror chain ships the GitHub OAuth token off-host to attacker C2. Rationale: Targets the smoking-gun network leg of Askar's PoC chain (cybersecuritynews.com/cyberpress.org confirm): malicious VS Code extension installed via the simulated-keypress trick reads the OAuth token POST'd by github.com to github.dev and ships it off-host. Legitimate code.exe traffic stays within Microsoft + GitHub + a small marketplace CDN footprint, so anything else is high-signal. Cross-checked: https://cybersecuritynews.com/1-click-github-token-vulnerability/, https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48371562. Cross-checked against: • https://cybersecuritynews.com/1-click-github-token-vulnerability/ • https://cyberpress.org/1-click-github-flaw/ • https://blog.ammaraskar.com/ • https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48371562

title: VS Code Process Outbound to Non-Microsoft/Non-GitHub Domain
id: 8c9d2f10-9b8e-4d6f-8f2a-3e1b2c4d5a01
status: experimental
description: VS Code (code.exe) connecting outbound to a destination outside the expected Microsoft / GitHub / extension marketplace footprint. Possible OAuth token exfiltration following the github.dev webview exploit chain disclosed by Ammar Askar (June 2026).
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/vs-code-zero-day-lets-hackers-steal-github-tokens-in-one-click/
  - https://blog.ammaraskar.com/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/03
tags:
  - attack.t1567
  - attack.t1539
  - attack.exfiltration
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\Code.exe'
      - '\code.exe'
    Initiated: 'true'
  selection_port:
    DestinationPort:
      - 80
      - 443
      - 8080
      - 8443
  filter_trusted:
    DestinationHostname|endswith:
      - '.github.com'
      - '.github.dev'
      - '.githubusercontent.com'
      - '.vscode-cdn.net'
      - '.visualstudio.com'
      - '.microsoft.com'
      - '.azureedge.net'
      - '.trafficmanager.net'
      - '.vscode-unpkg.net'
      - '.vsassets.io'
  filter_empty_host:
    DestinationHostname: ''
  condition: selection_image and selection_port and not (filter_trusted or filter_empty_host)
falsepositives:
  - Marketplace updates served from non-Microsoft CDNs
  - Language-server downloads (Pylance, gopls, rust-analyzer)
  - GitHub Copilot or third-party extension telemetry
level: medium
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @Image:(*\\Code.exe OR *\\code.exe OR *\\CODE.EXE) @DestinationPort:(80 OR 443 OR 8080 OR 8443) -@DestinationHostname:(*github.com OR *github.dev OR *githubusercontent.com OR *vscode-cdn.net OR *visualstudio.com OR *microsoft.com OR *azureedge.net OR *trafficmanager.net OR *vscode-unpkg.net)
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest
| ContextImageFileName=/\\Code\.exe$/i
| NOT regex("(github\\.com|github\\.dev|githubusercontent\\.com|vscode-cdn\\.net|visualstudio\\.com|microsoft\\.com|azureedge\\.net|trafficmanager\\.net|vscode-unpkg\\.net)$", field=DomainName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, DomainName], function=count())
| count > 0
CLOUD

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.dest_port) as ports from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.app="code.exe" AND All_Traffic.dest_port IN (80,443,8080,8443) by host, All_Traffic.user, All_Traffic.app, All_Traffic.dest | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | where NOT match(dest, "(github\\.com|github\\.dev|githubusercontent\\.com|vscode-cdn\\.net|visualstudio\\.com|microsoft\\.com|azureedge\\.net|vscode-sync\\.trafficmanager\\.net|vscode-unpkg\\.net|openvsxorg\\.blob\\.core\\.windows\\.net|vsmarketplacebadges\\.dev)$") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
[LLM] VS Code extension file write within 120s of opening a .ipynb notebook (one-click install chain) Installation High
Correlates code.exe opening a .ipynb Jupyter notebook file with code.exe writing files into %USERPROFILE%\.vscode\extensions\ within 120 seconds. This is the fingerprint of Askar's exploit: a poisoned .ipynb fires an <img onerror> handler inside the webview, the JS uses postMessage + synthesised did-keydown events to drive the Extensions UI silently, and a malicious extension lands on disk with no real user interaction. Rationale: Directly targets the choke point in Askar's chain: the .ipynb-onerror webview-escape PoC ends with a malicious extension dropped on disk via simulated keypresses, and the 120-second window separates that automated drop from a human browsing the marketplace (which typically takes minutes and is not preceded by opening a notebook). Notebook file open and extension write both come from code.exe, so the InitiatingProcess pivot keeps the join tight. Confirmed in cybersecuritynews.com and cyberpress.org write-ups which explicitly call out the .ipynb+onerror+webview chain. Cross-checked against: • https://cybersecuritynews.com/1-click-github-token-vulnerability/ • https://cyberpress.org/1-click-github-flaw/ • https://gbhackers.com/1-click-github-vulnerability/ • https://blog.ammaraskar.com/
ATT&CKT1176 T1059.007 T1204.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
let WindowSec = 120s;
let Notebooks = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "code.exe"
    | where FileName endswith ".ipynb"
    | where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
    | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NotebookTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName, NotebookPath = FolderPath, NotebookName = FileName, NotebookSrc = FileOriginUrl;
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "code.exe"
| where FolderPath has @"\.vscode\extensions\"
| where ActionType == "FileCreated"
| where FileName in~ ("package.json","extension.js","extension.vsix")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project ExtWriteTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, ExtAccount = InitiatingProcessAccountName, ExtFolderPath = FolderPath, ExtFileName = FileName
| join kind=inner Notebooks on DeviceId
| where ExtAccount =~ AccountName
| where ExtWriteTime between (NotebookTime .. NotebookTime + WindowSec)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', ExtWriteTime, NotebookTime)
| project NotebookTime, ExtWriteTime, DelaySec, DeviceName, AccountName, NotebookName, NotebookPath, NotebookSrc, ExtFolderPath, ExtFileName
| order by NotebookTime desc
let WindowSec = 120s;
let Notebooks = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessName endswith @"\Code.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith @"\code.exe"
    | where TargetFileName endswith ".ipynb"
    | where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
    | project NotebookTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, NotebookPath = TargetFilePath, NotebookName = TargetFileName;
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith @"\Code.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith @"\code.exe"
| where TargetFilePath has @"\.vscode\extensions\"
| where EventType == "FileCreated"
| where TargetFileName in~ ("package.json","extension.js","extension.vsix")
| project ExtWriteTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ExtPath = TargetFilePath, ExtFile = TargetFileName
| join kind=inner Notebooks on DvcHostname, ActorUsername
| where ExtWriteTime between (NotebookTime .. NotebookTime + WindowSec)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', ExtWriteTime, NotebookTime)
| project NotebookTime, ExtWriteTime, DelaySec, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, NotebookName, NotebookPath, ExtPath, ExtFile
| order by NotebookTime desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @Image:(*\\Code.exe OR *\\code.exe) @TargetFilename:(*\\.vscode\\extensions\\* OR *\\.vscode\\Extensions\\*) @TargetFilename:(*package.json OR *extension.js OR *extension.vsix)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| ContextImageFileName=/\\Code\.exe$/i
| regex("\\\\\\.vscode\\\\extensions\\\\", field=TargetFileName)
| TargetFileName=/(package\.json|extension\.js|extension\.vsix)$/i
| join({#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo | ContextImageFileName=/\\Code\.exe$/i | TargetFileName=/\.ipynb$/i | rename(_time, as=NotebookTime)}, field=aid, include=[NotebookTime])
| ExtWriteTime := _time
| DelaySec := ExtWriteTime - NotebookTime
| DelaySec > 0
| DelaySec < 120
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName], function={ min(NotebookTime, as=NotebookOpenedAt) | min(ExtWriteTime, as=ExtensionWrittenAt) | min(DelaySec, as=GapSeconds) })

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as ipynbTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as notebook_paths from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.process_name="code.exe" AND Filesystem.file_name="*.ipynb" by host, Filesystem.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | rename user as victim_user | join host victim_user [ | tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as extWriteTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as extension_paths from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.process_name="code.exe" AND Filesystem.file_path="*\\.vscode\\extensions\\*" AND (Filesystem.file_name="package.json" OR Filesystem.file_name="extension.js" OR Filesystem.file_name="extension.vsix") by host, Filesystem.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | rename user as victim_user ] | eval delta_seconds=extWriteTime-ipynbTime | where delta_seconds > 0 AND delta_seconds < 120 | `security_content_ctime(ipynbTime)` | `security_content_ctime(extWriteTime)`
[LLM] Mass GitHub private repository enumeration in short window (stolen OAuth token reuse) Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects a single GitHub identity reading/listing more private repositories than a real developer ever would inside a 5-minute window. This is the actions-on-objectives stage of Askar's exploit: the unscoped github.dev OAuth token grants full access to every repo the victim can see, and the PoC explicitly enumerates them via the GitHub API. Rationale: Article explicitly states the PoC 'queries the GitHub API to enumerate all private repositories the victim can access.' The github.dev OAuth token, per Askar, 'is not scoped to the particular repo... it has full access to every other repo,' so an attacker will fan out across all reachable repos within seconds — a shape no organic developer produces. Threshold + burst-duration combo distinguishes from slow background tooling. Cross-checked the unscoped-token claim against cybersecuritynews.com and the GitHub blog spotlight on Askar. Cross-checked against: • https://cybersecuritynews.com/1-click-github-token-vulnerability/ • https://github.blog/security/vulnerability-research/cybersecurity-spotlight-on-bug-bounty-researcher-ammar-askar/ • https://blog.ammaraskar.com/
ATT&CKT1213.003 T1083 T1539
Data sourcesWeb.Web
let WindowMin = 5m;
let RepoThreshold = 25;
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application has "GitHub"
| where ActionType in~ ("RepositoryReadAccess","List user repositories","List organization repositories","Get repository","git.clone","git.fetch","Repository_Cloned")

Weedhack Attacks Minecraft Users, CountLoader Hits 86K, Miners Spread via Pirated Content

The Hacker News
2026-06-03 19 use cases 9 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

Cybersecurity researchers have flagged a new campaign targeting Minecraft players via YouTube to spread malware capable of gaining control of victims' systems. The Minecraft-focused malware-as-a-service (MaaS) campaign has been codenamed Weedhack by McAfee Labs, stating the activity has been active since January 2026 and impersonates Minecraft clients and mods to infect users. In all, 3820

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Weedhack DonutDupe.jar launched via java.exe (Minecraft MaaS first stage) · [LLM] CountLoader: EXE → PowerShell → mshta.exe obfuscated JS chain · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Weedhack Attacks Minecraft Users, CountLoader Hits 86K, Miners Spread via Pirate
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Weedhack multi-stage JAR drops: Elevator/SecurityManager/Component.jar · [LLM] Pirated-miner DLL side-load via HLS Installer.874.exe · [LLM] Pirated-miner: Defender exclusion add + MRT.exe termination + sleep disable · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Weedhack C2 dashboard contact: outbound to weedhack[.]to · [LLM] Weedhack EtherHiding: java.exe contacts public Ethereum RPC endpoints · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] CountLoader USB propagation: scripts/EXEs written to removable media · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
[LLM] Weedhack DonutDupe.jar launched via java.exe (Minecraft MaaS first stage) Delivery High
Catches java.exe (or javaw.exe) executing the article's first-stage JAR 'DonutDupe.jar' dropped from a malicious Minecraft mod/client site. Article-specific binary + parent-child shape, distinct from generic javaw activity. Rationale: DonutDupe.jar is the named first-stage from McAfee's Weedhack writeup; java/javaw executing a file literally containing that string is extremely high-fidelity. Minecraft launchers normally invoke launcher-specific JARs (minecraft.jar, forge-*.jar), not files containing 'DonutDupe'. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/weedhack-attacks-minecraft-users.html
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("java.exe","javaw.exe","javaws.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "DonutDupe" and ProcessCommandLine has ".jar"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\java.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\javaw.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\javaws.exe"
| where CommandLine has "DonutDupe" and CommandLine has ".jar"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Weedhack DonutDupe.jar Executed via Java
id: 5b2a7c1e-9a1f-4b2c-8d3a-6e1a7c5b9d11
description: Detects java/javaw/javaws executing the Weedhack first-stage payload DonutDupe.jar.

[LLM] Weedhack C2 dashboard contact: outbound to weedhack[.]to Command & Control High
DNS or HTTP contact with weedhack[.]to, the clear-net dashboard that operators use to view stolen credentials and command Weedhack-infected hosts. Domain is the central operational artefact of the campaign. Rationale: weedhack[.]to is the only named domain in the McAfee writeup — it is the operator dashboard, so any resolution from an enterprise host is by-definition an infection. Single-IOC, single-event detection. Fixed Sentinel schema: switched from DeviceName (Defender-only) to Computer/ClientIP on DnsEvents, SrcHostname on ImDnsActivity/ImWebSession, and SourceHostName on CommonSecurityLog. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/weedhack-attacks-minecraft-users.html
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
union
( DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where RemoteUrl has "weedhack.to"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort ),
( DeviceEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse"
  | where AdditionalFields has "weedhack.to"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, AdditionalFields )
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
( DnsEvents
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where Name has "weedhack.to"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, ResultCode ),
( ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DnsQuery has "weedhack.to"
  | project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DnsQuery, DnsResponseCodeName, DvcHostname ),
( ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where Url has "weedhack.to" or DstHostname has "weedhack.to"
  | project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, Url, DvcHostname ),
( CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where RequestURL has "weedhack.to" or DestinationHostName has "weedhack.to"
  | project TimeGenerated, SourceHostName, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, RequestURL )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Weedhack EtherHiding: java.exe contacts public Ethereum RPC endpoints Command & Control Medium
Detects Java processes (the Weedhack JAR chain) issuing JSON-RPC to public Ethereum nodes — the EtherHiding technique used to fetch the next-stage C2 server. Java reaching an Ethereum mainnet RPC is essentially never legitimate in an enterprise environment. Rationale: Article explicitly cites EtherHiding (Ethereum blockchain as dead-drop resolver) for the DonutDupe→C2 hop. Sentinel ASIM ImNetworkSession lacks process attribution, so we join SecurityEvent 4688 (java.exe spawns) to ImNetworkSession on Computer+30-minute window. Fixed prior schema error: removed ActingProcessName/ActingProcessCommandLine from ImNetworkSession (those are ImProcessCreate fields). Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/weedhack-attacks-minecraft-users.html • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1102/
ATT&CKT1102 T1568
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
let EthRpc = dynamic(["mainnet.infura.io","cloudflare-eth.com","rpc.ankr.com","eth-mainnet.g.alchemy.com","eth.llamarpc.com","ethereum.publicnode.com","rpc.flashbots.net","api.etherscan.io"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("java.exe","javaw.exe","javaws.exe")
| where RemoteUrl has_any (EthRpc) or tostring(parse_url(RemoteUrl).Host) has_any (EthRpc)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
let EthRpc = dynamic(["mainnet.infura.io","cloudflare-eth.com","rpc.ankr.com","eth-mainnet.g.alchemy.com","eth.llamarpc.com","ethereum.publicnode.com","rpc.flashbots.net","api.etherscan.io"]);
let JavaProcs = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where NewProcessName endswith "\\java.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\javaw.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\javaws.exe"
    | project ProcStart=TimeGenerated, Computer, NewProcessId, NewProcessName, CommandLine;
let EthNet = union isfuzzy=true
    ( ImNetworkSession
      | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
      | where DstHostname has_any (EthRpc) or Url has_any (EthRpc)
      | project NetTime=TimeGenerated, Host=coalesce(SrcHostname, DvcHostname), DstHostname, Url, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber ),
    ( ImWebSession
      | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
      | where Url has_any (EthRpc) or DstHostname has_any (EthRpc)

[LLM] Weedhack multi-stage JAR drops: Elevator/SecurityManager/Component.jar Installation High
File-create events for the three follow-on Weedhack JARs (Elevator.jar, SecurityManager.jar, Component.jar) written to disk after DonutDupe.jar runs. These exact names are stage-2/3/4 in the article's chain and are not legitimate Minecraft artefacts. Rationale: Article names these three JARs as Weedhack's stage-2 (Elevator), stage-3 persistence (SecurityManager), and stage-4 RAT (Component). The names 'SecurityManager.jar' and 'Component.jar' especially are deliberately innocuous-sounding but are not standard Minecraft / Forge / Fabric artefacts. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/weedhack-attacks-minecraft-users.html

| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)

[LLM] CountLoader: EXE → PowerShell → mshta.exe obfuscated JS chain Delivery High
Detects the CountLoader execution chain described in the article: an EXE launches a PowerShell command that downloads/executes an obfuscated JS loader via mshta.exe. Targets the three-process tree shape (EXE→powershell→mshta) that's distinctive vs ordinary mshta usage. Rationale: Article explicitly states 'The loader is executed using mshta.exe' and 'PowerShell command, which downloads and executes an obfuscated JavaScript loader'. The PowerShell→mshta parent→child relationship is the article-specific signature; mshta launched from cmd.exe/explorer.exe is normal-ish, but launched from powershell with a URL/javascript: arg is the CountLoader pattern. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/weedhack-attacks-minecraft-users.html • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1218/005/
ATT&CKT1218.005 T1059.001 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "mshta.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(javascript:|vbscript:|http[s]?://|\.hta\b|new\s+ActiveXObject|WScript\.Shell)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\mshta.exe"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\powershell.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(javascript:|vbscript:|http[s]?://|\.hta\b|new\s+ActiveXObject|WScript\.Shell)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] CountLoader USB propagation: scripts/EXEs written to removable media Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects CountLoader's USB-spreading behaviour — writes of .js / .hta / .lnk / autorun.inf / .exe to removable drives by a process recently associated with the loader chain. Article attributes ~9,000 of the 86,000 CountLoader infections to USB spread. Rationale: Article specifies CountLoader 'attempts to spread via USB drives' and that ~9k of 86k infections came from USB/removable media. Combination of removable-drive root path + LNK/HTA/JS/autorun.inf + non-Explorer writer is the classic USB-worm shape and isolates from legitimate user file copies. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/weedhack-attacks-minecraft-users.html • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1091/
ATT&CKT1091 T1547.009
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath matches regex @"^[D-Z]:\\"
| where FileName =~ "autorun.inf" or FileName endswith ".lnk" or FileName endswith ".hta" or FileName endswith ".js" or FileName endswith ".vbs"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("explorer.exe","OneDrive.exe","Dropbox.exe","GoogleDriveFS.exe")
| summarize FileCount=dcount(FileName), Files=make_set(FileName,20), SamplePath=any(FolderPath), arg_max(Timestamp,*) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, bin(Timestamp,5m)
| where FileCount >= 2
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileCreate","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFilePath matches regex @"^[D-Z]:\\"
| where TargetFileName =~ "autorun.inf" or TargetFileExtension in~ ("lnk","hta","js","vbs")
| where ActingProcessName !endswith "\\explorer.exe" and ActingProcessName !endswith "\\OneDrive.exe"
| summarize FileCount=dcount(TargetFileName), Files=make_set(TargetFileName,20), arg_max(TimeGenerated,*) by DvcHostname, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, bin(TimeGenerated,5m)
| where FileCount >= 2
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @TargetFilename:(D\:\\* OR E\:\\* OR F\:\\* OR G\:\\* OR H\:\\*) @TargetFilename:(*autorun.inf OR *.lnk OR *.hta OR *.js OR *.vbs) -@Image:(*\explorer.exe OR *\OneDrive.exe OR *\Dropbox.exe)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/^[D-Z]:\\/i TargetFileName=/(autorun\.inf|\.lnk|\.hta|\.js|\.vbs)$/i
| ContextImageFileName!=/\\(explorer|OneDrive|Dropbox)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
| count > 1

[LLM] Pirated-miner DLL side-load via HLS Installer.874.exe Installation High
Detects the article's miner-delivery vector: legitimate 'HLS Installer.874.exe' loading a non-Microsoft DLL from its working directory — the side-loading mechanism that injects the SilentCryptoMiner-fork loader. Tracks both the process launch and the suspicious image load. Rationale: Kaspersky's writeup (cited in article) names exactly 'HLS Installer.874.exe' as the legitimate side-load host for the SilentCryptoMiner fork. The filename is too specific to occur by chance; any execution from a host that touched a pirated-streaming site should be treated as the miner installer. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/weedhack-attacks-minecraft-users.html
ATT&CKT1574.002 T1496
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
let HlsProcs = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(90d)
    | where FileName =~ "HLS Installer.874.exe"
    | project ProcTime=Timestamp, DeviceName, ProcessId, FolderPath, AccountName, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine;
let SideLoads = DeviceImageLoadEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(90d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "HLS Installer.874.exe"
    | where FolderPath !startswith "C:\\Windows\\" and FolderPath !startswith "C:\\Program Files\\"
    | where InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName != "Microsoft Corporation"
    | project LoadTime=Timestamp, DeviceName, LoadedDll=FileName, LoadedPath=FolderPath, LoadedSHA256=SHA256, InitiatingProcessId;
HlsProcs
| union SideLoads
| order by coalesce(ProcTime, LoadTime) desc
union isfuzzy=true
( SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
  | where EventID == 4688
  | where NewProcessName endswith "HLS Installer.874.exe" or CommandLine has "HLS Installer.874.exe"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName ),
( ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
  | where ActingProcessName endswith "HLS Installer.874.exe" or TargetProcessName endswith "HLS Installer.874.exe"
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Pirated-miner: Defender exclusion add + MRT.exe termination + sleep disable Installation High
Catches the SilentCryptoMiner-fork defence-evasion stack: process adds Microsoft Defender path/process exclusions, then terminates MRT.exe (Malicious Software Removal Tool), then disables hibernation/sleep via powercfg — three article-named actions in a short window. Rationale: Article explicitly lists, as miner capabilities: 'Configure Defender exclusions, terminate Microsoft's Malicious Software Removal Tool, and disable automatic hibernation and sleep mode'. Each action alone is sometimes legitimate; the combination on the same host within 30 minutes is uniquely article-shaped and rare in benign IT activity. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/weedhack-attacks-minecraft-users.html • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1562/001/
ATT&CKT1562.001 T1562.012
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let Win = 30m;
let DefenderEx = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Add-MpPreference","Set-MpPreference")
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("ExclusionPath","ExclusionProcess","ExclusionExtension","DisableRealtimeMonitoring","DisableBehaviorMonitoring")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, EvtType="DefenderExclusion";
let MrtKill = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where (FileName =~ "taskkill.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "MRT")
         or (FileName =~ "sc.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "MRT")
         or (FileName =~ "powershell.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "Stop-Process" and ProcessCommandLine has "MRT")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, EvtType="MRTKill";
let PowerCfg = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FileName =~ "powercfg.exe"
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("hibernate off","standby-timeout","monitor-timeout","-h off")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, EvtType="PowerCfg";
DefenderEx | union MrtKill, PowerCfg
| summarize EvtTypes=make_set(EvtType), Cmds=make_set(ProcessCommandLine,10), arg_max(Timestamp,*) by DeviceName, bin(Timestamp, Win)
| where array_length(EvtTypes) >= 2
| order by Timestamp desc
let Win = 30m;
let Procs = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | extend EvtType = case(
        CommandLine has_any ("Add-MpPreference","Set-MpPreference") and CommandLine has_any ("ExclusionPath","ExclusionProcess","DisableRealtimeMonitoring"), "DefenderExclusion",
        (NewProcessName endswith "\\taskkill.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\sc.exe") and CommandLine has "MRT", "MRTKill",
        NewProcessName endswith "\\powershell.exe" and CommandLine has "Stop-Process" and CommandLine has "MRT", "MRTKill",
        NewProcessName endswith "\\powercfg.exe" and CommandLine has_any ("hibernate off","standby-timeout","monitor-timeout","-h off"), "PowerCfg",
        "")
    | where EvtType != ""
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, EvtType;
Procs
| summarize EvtTypes=make_set(EvtType), Cmds=make_set(CommandLine,10), arg_max(TimeGenerated,*) by Computer, bin(TimeGenerated, Win)
| where array_length(EvtTypes) >= 2
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@CommandLine:(*Add-MpPreference*ExclusionPath* OR *Add-MpPreference*ExclusionProcess* OR *Set-MpPreference*DisableRealtimeMonitoring*) OR (@CommandLine:*MRT* AND @Image:(*\taskkill.exe OR *\sc.exe)) OR (@Image:(*\powercfg.exe OR *\POWERCFG.EXE) AND @CommandLine:(*hibernate*off* OR *standby-timeout*0* OR *monitor-timeout*0* OR *-h*off*)))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 (CommandLine=/Add-MpPreference.*Exclusion(Path|Process|Extension)/i OR CommandLine=/Set-MpPreference.*DisableRealtimeMonitoring/i OR (ImageFileName=/\\(taskkill|sc)\.exe$/i CommandLine=/\bMRT\b/i) OR (ImageFileName=/\\powercfg\.exe$/i CommandLine=/(hibernate\s+off|standby-timeout|monitor-timeout|-h\s+off)/i))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process="*Add-MpPreference*ExclusionPath*" OR Processes.process="*Add-MpPreference*ExclusionProcess*" OR Processes.process="*Set-MpPreference*DisableRealtimeMonitoring*" OR (Processes.process="*taskkill*" AND Processes.process="*MRT*") OR (Processes.process_name="powercfg.exe" AND (Processes.process="*hibernate*off*" OR Processes.process="*-change*standby-timeout*0*" OR Processes.process="*monitor-timeout*0*"))) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name _time | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | sort 0 - _time
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Preinstall to persistence: Inside the Red Hat npm Miasma credential-stealing campaign

Microsoft Security Blog
2026-06-03 20 use cases 6 techniques 7 kill-chain phases detected

A large-scale npm supply chain attack compromised over 90 versions of @redhat-cloud-services packages, silently infecting CI/CD environments and developer systems. The malicious code steals credentials from GitHub, cloud platforms, and local machines, then spreads like a worm by republishing trusted packages. Discover how the attack works, what data is at risk, and the steps you can take to protect your organization. The post Preinstall to persistence: Inside the Red Hat npm Miasma credential-stealing campaign appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog .

ATT&CKT1027 T1190 T1195.002 T1204.002 T1486 T1528
SHA2567069e28a5806db4a… b86c5ae9e95bd841…

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Passwordless sudo rule dropped into /etc/sudoers.d (Miasma privilege escalation) · [LLM] Security vendor domain blackhole written to /etc/hosts from non-admin process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Preinstall to persistence: Inside the Red Hat npm Miasma credential-stealing cam
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Bun runtime spawned via node→shell→bun chain from npm install (Miasma dropper) · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] GitHub Actions Runner.Worker process-memory secret scraping (Miasma payload) · [LLM] Cloud IMDS credential harvesting from node/bun process on CI runner · [LLM] Public GitHub repo creation matching Miasma 'adjective-creature-N' exfil pattern · [LLM] Worm-injected .github/setup.js commit with 'chore: update dependencies [skip ci]' message · [LLM] Destructive 'rm -rf ~' or Miasma honeytoken tripwire from node/bun process tree · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft)
[LLM] Bun runtime spawned via node→shell→bun chain from npm install (Miasma dropper) Installation High
Hunts the signature process tree of the Red Hat npm Miasma campaign: a node.js process spawning a shell that spawns the Bun runtime, typically from npm preinstall hooks. This is the exact anti-Node-monitoring evasion chain the article identifies for the 4.29 MB index.js dropper. Rationale: Anchored on the article's exact statement: 'creating an unusual process chain (node → shell → bun → payload) designed to evade Node-focused monitoring.' The Bun runtime is downloaded to a temp path before execution, and bun is not a standard CI runner tool — the parent-of-parent being node/npm in a preinstall context is article-specific.
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1546.016 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("bun", "bun.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("node","node.exe","npm","npm-cli.js","yarn","pnpm")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("preinstall","npm install","index.js")
| where FolderPath startswith "/tmp/" or FolderPath startswith "/home/runner/" or FolderPath has "/.bun/" or FolderPath has @"\AppData\Local\Temp\" or FolderPath has "/var/folders/"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
    ParentFile = InitiatingProcessFileName, ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
    GrandparentFile = InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "bun" or ActingProcessName endswith "bun.exe"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "sh" or ParentProcessName endswith "bash" or ParentProcessName endswith "cmd.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "powershell.exe"
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("node","npm","preinstall","index.js")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/tmp/","/home/runner/","/.bun/",@"\AppData\Local\Temp\","/var/folders/")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Bun Runtime Spawned by Node Shell Chain (Miasma npm Dropper)
id: a3f9d8e2-7b41-4c5a-9e2d-1f8b6c3a9d77
description: Detects the node → shell → bun process chain characteristic of the Red Hat npm Miasma supply chain campaign, where a preinstall hook executes a 4.29 MB index.js dropper that downloads and detonates the Bun runtime.
references:
  - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/02/preinstall-persistence-inside-red-hat-npm-miasma-credential-stealing-campaign/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/03
tags:
  - attack.t1059.007
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.t1546.016
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bun'
      - '/bun.exe'
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/sh'
      - '/bash'
      - '/dash'
      - '/zsh'
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
  selection_grandparent_or_path:
    - ParentCommandLine|contains:
        - 'node'
        - 'npm'
        - 'preinstall'
        - 'index.js'
    - Image|contains:
        - '/tmp/'
        - '/home/runner/'
        - '/.bun/'
        - '\Temp\'
        - '/var/folders/'
  condition: selection_image and selection_parent and selection_grandparent_or_path
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate developer use of Bun in npm scripts (rare in CI baseline)
  - Bun installer running interactively (curl https://bun.sh/install | bash)
level: high
source:(linux.auditd OR windows.sysmon) @auditd.type:EXECVE (@process.name:bun OR @process.name:bun.exe OR @Image:(*\bun OR *\bun.exe OR */bun OR */bun.exe)) (@process.parent.name:(sh OR bash OR dash OR zsh OR cmd.exe OR powershell.exe) OR @ParentImage:(*\sh OR *\bash OR *\cmd.exe OR *\powershell.exe)) (@process.command_line:(*node* OR *npm* OR *preinstall* OR *index.js*) OR @ParentCommandLine:(*node* OR *npm* OR *preinstall* OR *index.js*)) (@process.executable.path:(*/tmp/* OR */home/runner/* OR */.bun/* OR */var/folders/*) OR @Image:(*\Temp\* OR */tmp/* OR */.bun/*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\/bun(\.exe)?$/i
| ParentBaseFileName=/^(sh|bash|dash|zsh|cmd\.exe|powershell\.exe)$/i
| regex("(node|npm|preinstall|index\\.js)", field=ParentCommandLine)
| regex("(\/tmp\/|\/home\/runner\/|\.bun\/|\\\\Temp\\\\|\/var\/folders\/)", field=ImageFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName, ParentCommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT

[LLM] GitHub Actions Runner.Worker process-memory secret scraping (Miasma payload) Actions on Objectives High
Hunts the Miasma payload's runtime-secret theft technique: scanning /proc/<pid>/cmdline for 'Runner.Worker' to locate the GitHub Actions worker PID, then extracting masked Actions secrets from process memory via a distinctive grep regex for '"isSecret":true' JSON tokens. Rationale: Anchored on the article's verbatim code block: 'findRunnerWorkerPIDLinux', the exact extraction regex 'grep -aoE \'"[^"]+":{"value":"[^"]*","isSecret":true}\'', and the /proc/<pid>/cmdline scan strategy. These strings have no legitimate occurrence outside this campaign and the article explicitly cites them as the runner-memory exfiltration mechanism.
ATT&CKT1003 T1552.005 T1057
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Runner.Worker", "findRunnerWorkerPIDLinux", "\"isSecret\":true")
   or (ProcessCommandLine has "grep" and ProcessCommandLine has "-aoE" and ProcessCommandLine has "/proc/" and ProcessCommandLine has "cmdline")
   or (ProcessCommandLine has "/proc/" and ProcessCommandLine has "cmdline" and ProcessCommandLine has "tr -d")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("runner-worker","Runner.Listener","actions.runner")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
    InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("Runner.Worker", "findRunnerWorkerPIDLinux", "\"isSecret\":true")
   or (ActingProcessCommandLine has "grep" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "-aoE" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "/proc/" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "cmdline")
| where ParentProcessName !endswith "Runner.Listener"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Cloud IMDS credential harvesting from node/bun process on CI runner Actions on Objectives High
Detects short-lived node or bun processes contacting the AWS/Azure IMDS (169.254.169.254) or GCP metadata service (metadata.google.internal) — the Miasma payload's mechanism for stealing instance role credentials, Azure IMDS OAuth2 tokens, and GCP service-account tokens from CI runners. Rationale: Anchored on the article's credential-theft section listing exact endpoints: 'IMDS (169.254.169.254)', 'metadata.google.internal service-account tokens', and 'IMDS OAuth2 tokens for management.azure.com, graph.microsoft.com, and Key Vault (*.vault.azure.net)'. Node/bun calling IMDS from a CI runner is the article's specific behavior — the article notes Linux CI runners as the primary target.
ATT&CKT1552.005 T1528 T1552.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP == "169.254.169.254" or RemoteUrl has_any ("metadata.google.internal", "169.254.169.254", "metadata.azure.com", ".vault.azure.net")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","node.exe","bun","bun.exe")
| summarize EndpointsHit = make_set(RemoteUrl), IPHits = make_set(RemoteIP), HitCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
    by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| where HitCount >= 1
| order by FirstSeen desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr == "169.254.169.254" or DstHostname has_any ("metadata.google.internal","metadata.azure.com",".vault.azure.net")
| where Url has_any ("node","bun") or DstHostname has_any ("metadata","vault.azure")
| summarize EndpointsHit = make_set(DstHostname), HitCount = count() by DvcHostname, SrcUsername, NetworkApplicationProtocol
| order by HitCount desc
title: Cloud IMDS Access by Node or Bun Process (Miasma Harvester)
id: 8b1c4e72-5d39-4f86-a2b1-7e3c9f5a4d18
description: Detects node or bun processes contacting cloud instance metadata endpoints (AWS IMDS 169.254.169.254, GCP metadata.google.internal, Azure IMDS, Key Vault) to harvest temporary cloud credentials. Specific to the Red Hat npm Miasma campaign on CI runners and developer hosts.
references:
  - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/02/preinstall-persistence-inside-red-hat-npm-miasma-credential-stealing-campaign/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/03
tags:
  - attack.t1552.005
  - attack.t1528
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_process:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/node'
      - '/bun'
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\bun.exe'
  selection_dest:
    DestinationIp:
      - '169.254.169.254'
    DestinationHostname|contains:
      - 'metadata.google.internal'
      - 'metadata.azure.com'
      - '.vault.azure.net'
  condition: selection_process and selection_dest
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate Node.js apps using AWS SDK / Azure SDK that resolve IMDS for instance role credentials
  - Bun-based serverless adapters that intentionally call IMDS
level: high
source:(linux.auditd OR windows.sysmon OR cloudtrail) (@network.destination.ip:169.254.169.254 OR @DestinationIp:169.254.169.254 OR @network.destination.host:(metadata.google.internal OR metadata.azure.com) OR @DestinationHostname:(metadata.google.internal OR *.vault.azure.net)) (@process.name:(node OR bun) OR @Image:(*\node.exe OR *\bun.exe OR */node OR */bun))
(#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 OR #event_simpleName=DnsRequest)
| (RemoteAddressIP4="169.254.169.254" OR DomainName=/metadata\.(google\.internal|azure\.com)/i OR DomainName=/.*\.vault\.azure\.net$/i)
| ContextImageFileName=/\/(node|bun)(\.exe)?$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, ContextProcessId, DomainName, RemoteAddressIP4], function=count())
# log group: /aws/vpc/flowlogs
fields @timestamp, srcAddr, dstAddr, dstPort, action, bytes
| filter dstAddr = "169.254.169.254"
      and action = "ACCEPT"
| stats count(*) as imdsCalls, sum(bytes) as totalBytes by srcAddr, bin(5m)
| sort @timestamp desc
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest="169.254.169.254" OR All_Traffic.dest_host="metadata.google.internal") AND (All_Traffic.process_name="node" OR All_Traffic.process_name="node.exe" OR All_Traffic.process_name="bun" OR All_Traffic.process_name="bun.exe") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_host All_Traffic.process_name All_Traffic.process | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest="169.254.169.254" OR All_Traffic.dest_host="metadata.google.internal") AND (All_Traffic.process_name="node" OR All_Traffic.process_name="node.exe" OR All_Traffic.process_name="bun" OR All_Traffic.process_name="bun.exe") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_host All_Traffic.process_name All_Traffic.process | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
[LLM] Passwordless sudo rule dropped into /etc/sudoers.d (Miasma privilege escalation) Exploitation High
Detects creation of files under /etc/sudoers.d containing 'NOPASSWD:ALL' (specifically the 'runner ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL' string the Miasma payload writes), and the bind-mount-to-/mnt technique used to deposit the sudoers fragment. Sigma covers the process-create path; KQL covers both file-write and sudoers-validation chains. Rationale: Anchored on the article's exact verbatim code block: "echo 'runner ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL' > ... && chmod 0440 /mnt/runner" and "sudo -n true". The 'NOPASSWD:ALL' string combined with a /etc/sudoers.d or /mnt/ write target is the article-specific signature; this rule should not fire on legitimate config-mgmt because we filter on node/bun/shell parents.
ATT&CKT1548.003 T1098
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
union
  (DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "NOPASSWD:ALL"
       and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/etc/sudoers.d","/mnt/","sudoers")
    | extend Source = "ProcessCreate"),
  (DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FolderPath startswith "/etc/sudoers.d/"
       or (FolderPath startswith "/mnt/" and FileName has_any ("runner","sudoers"))
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","bun","sh","bash","dash","tee","cp","mv","dd")
    | extend Source = "FileWrite", ProcessCommandLine = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName_proc = InitiatingProcessFileName)
| project Timestamp, Source, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
union
  (ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "NOPASSWD:ALL"
       and ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/etc/sudoers.d","/mnt/","sudoers")
    | extend Source = "ProcessCreate"),
  (ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where TargetFilePath startswith "/etc/sudoers.d/"
       or (TargetFilePath startswith "/mnt/" and TargetFileName has_any ("runner","sudoers"))
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("node","bun","sh","bash","tee")
    | extend Source = "FileWrite", ActingProcessCommandLine = ActingProcessCommandLine)
| project TimeGenerated, Source, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Passwordless Sudo Rule Drop via /etc/sudoers.d (Miasma)
id: c4f2a51d-86b3-4c19-9e7a-2d8b6f3c4a91
description: Detects the Miasma payload writing 'NOPASSWD:ALL' rules into /etc/sudoers.d (often via a bind-mount of /mnt), granting passwordless root to the runner/maintainer account.
references:
  - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/02/preinstall-persistence-inside-red-hat-npm-miasma-credential-stealing-campaign/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/03
tags:
  - attack.t1548.003
  - attack.t1098
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains: 'NOPASSWD:ALL'
  selection_target:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/etc/sudoers.d'
      - '/mnt/'
      - 'sudoers'
  filter_pkg_install:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/apt'
      - '/dpkg'
      - '/yum'
      - '/dnf'
      - '/rpm'
  condition: selection_cmd and selection_target and not filter_pkg_install
falsepositives:
  - Configuration management (Ansible, Chef, Puppet) deploying sudoers fragments
  - Cloud-init / packer image bake steps writing CI runner sudo rules
level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.command_line:*NOPASSWD\:ALL* (@process.command_line:*\/etc\/sudoers.d* OR @process.command_line:*\/mnt\/* OR @process.command_line:*sudoers*) -@process.executable.path:(/usr/bin/apt OR /usr/bin/dpkg OR /usr/bin/yum OR /usr/bin/dnf) -@process.command_line:*ansible*
(#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 OR #event_simpleName=FileWritten)
| (regex("NOPASSWD:ALL", field=CommandLine) AND regex("(/etc/sudoers\\.d|/mnt/|sudoers)", field=CommandLine))
   OR (TargetFileName=/\/etc\/sudoers\.d\// OR TargetFileName=/\/mnt\/(runner|sudoers)/)
| ContextImageFileName=/\/(node|bun|sh|bash|tee|cp|dd)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process="*NOPASSWD:ALL*" AND (Processes.process="*/etc/sudoers.d*" OR Processes.process="*/mnt/*" OR Processes.process="*runner ALL=(ALL)*")) OR (Processes.process_name="mount" AND Processes.process="*bind*" AND Processes.process="*/etc/sudoers.d*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process="*NOPASSWD:ALL*" AND (Processes.process="*/etc/sudoers.d*" OR Processes.process="*/mnt/*" OR Processes.process="*runner ALL=(ALL)*")) OR (Processes.process_name="mount" AND Processes.process="*bind*" AND Processes.process="*/etc/sudoers.d*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
[LLM] Security vendor domain blackhole written to /etc/hosts from non-admin process Exploitation High
Detects the Miasma payload's defense-evasion step where it pipes 'echo 127.0.0.1 <vendor>' through sudo to append to /etc/hosts, blackholing telemetry/update domains for installed security products. Anchored on /etc/hosts writes initiated by node/bun/shell processes. Rationale: Anchored on the article's verbatim code block: 'sudo sh -c "echo \'127.0.0.1 <vendor>\' >> /etc/hosts"' under the Neutralize Security product monitoring comment. The combination of /etc/hosts + 127.0.0.1 + append from a node/bun/sh parent on a CI runner is highly article-specific.
ATT&CKT1562.001 T1565.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
union
  (DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "/etc/hosts"
       and ProcessCommandLine has "127.0.0.1"
       and ProcessCommandLine has_any (">>"," tee ","echo ")
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","bun","sh","bash","dash","zsh","sudo")
       or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("node","bun","npm")
    | extend Source = "ProcessCreate"),
  (DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FolderPath == "/etc/" and FileName == "hosts"
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","bun","sh","bash","dash","tee","sudo")
    | extend Source = "FileWrite", ProcessCommandLine = InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
| project Timestamp, Source, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
union
  (ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "/etc/hosts"
       and ActingProcessCommandLine has "127.0.0.1"
       and ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (">>"," tee ","echo ")
    | where ParentProcessName has_any ("node","bun","sh","bash","sudo")
    | extend Source = "ProcessCreate"),
  (ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where TargetFilePath == "/etc/hosts"
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("node","bun","sh","bash","tee")
    | extend Source = "FileWrite", ActingProcessCommandLine = ActingProcessCommandLine)
| project TimeGenerated, Source, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath
| order by TimeGenerated desc

id: 7e3a1b94-c52f-4d68-b1ae-9f4d8c2e7b15

[LLM] Public GitHub repo creation matching Miasma 'adjective-creature-N' exfil pattern Actions on Objectives High
Hunts the Miasma exfiltration channel: creation of a public GitHub repository under a victim's account named with the adjective-creature-N convention and/or containing the 'Miasma: The Spreading Blight' description, followed by commits to results/<timestamp>-<counter>.json paths. Pivots on CloudAppEvents / GitHub audit logs. Rationale: Anchored on Phase 10 of the article: 'Creates a public repo in the victim’s GitHub account ("Miasma: The Spreading Blight") and commits stolen credential JSON to results/<timestamp>-<counter>.json' and the adjective-creature-<0-99999> naming convention called out in the kill-chain reconstruction. Both the regex name pattern and the 'Miasma' string have no legitimate use in this org's GitHub footprint.
ATT&CKT1567.001 T1102.002
Data sourcesWeb
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where Application has "GitHub"
| where ActionType has_any ("Create repository","RepositoryCreate","repo.create")
| extend RepoName = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).repo)
| extend Visibility = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).visibility)
| extend Description = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).description)
| where Visibility =~ "public"
| where RepoName matches regex @"^[a-z]+-[a-z]+-\d{1,5}$"
   or Description has_any ("Miasma","Spreading Blight","The Spreading Blight")
   or RawEventData has "results/" and RawEventData has ".json"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, AccountObjectId, IPAddress, RepoName, Visibility, Description, RawEventData
| order by Timestamp desc
// Pre-req: GitHub Enterprise audit log connector ingesting into a custom GitHubAudit_CL table, or using OfficeActivity for GitHub via Cloud App Security
let GitHubLogs = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where OfficeWorkload has_any ("GitHub","github")
           or RecordType has "GitHub";
GitHubLogs
| where Operation has_any ("repo.create","RepositoryCreate","Create repository")
| extend RepoName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(EventData)).repo)
| extend Visibility = tostring(parse_json(tostring(EventData)).visibility)
| extend Description = tostring(parse_json(tostring(EventData)).description)
| where Visibility =~ "public"

   or Description has_any ("Miasma","Spreading Blight")

| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:github @action:(repo.create OR RepositoryCreate) @repo.visibility:public (@repo.name:/^[a-z]+-[a-z]+-\d{1,5}$/ OR @repo.description:(*Miasma* OR *"Spreading Blight"*))

[LLM] Worm-injected .github/setup.js commit with 'chore: update dependencies [skip ci]' message Actions on Objectives High
Detects the Miasma worm's lateral-movement technique: commits adding a .github/setup.js file via the GitHub Git Data API, authored as 'github-actions@github.com' with the verbatim message 'chore: update dependencies [skip ci]'. These commits appear across non-protected branches in victim-owned repos and skip CI by design. Rationale: Anchored on Phase 11 of the kill-chain reconstruction: 'Hunt for commits adding .github/setup.js authored as github-actions@github.com with message chore: update dependencies [skip ci]'. The exact file path, author email, and commit message are verbatim worm signatures with no legitimate corollary — Dependabot uses a different author identity and never adds setup.js.
ATT&CKT1080 T1195.002 T1098.004
Data sourcesChange
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where Application has "GitHub"
| where ActionType has_any ("git.push","push","PushCommit","Push")
| extend Files = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).added)
| extend Message = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).message)
| extend AuthorEmail = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).author_email)
| where Files has ".github/setup.js"
   or (Message =~ "chore: update dependencies [skip ci]" and AuthorEmail =~ "github-actions@github.com")
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, ObjectName, Files, Message, AuthorEmail, IPAddress, RawEventData
| order by Timestamp desc

   or (Message =~ "chore: update dependencies [skip ci]" and AuthorEmail =~ "github-actions@github.com")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, ObjectId, Files, Message, AuthorEmail, ClientIP
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Destructive 'rm -rf ~' or Miasma honeytoken tripwire from node/bun process tree Actions on Objectives High
Hunts the Miasma destructive fail-safe: 'rm -rf ~/' / 'rm -rf ~/Documents' invoked by a node or bun process tree (often after the planted honeytoken 'IfYouInvalidateThisTokenItWillNukeTheComputerOfTheOwner' is touched). Also directly matches the honeytoken string in any process command line or file content. Rationale: Anchored on Phase 12 of the kill-chain reconstruction: the verbatim honeytoken string 'IfYouInvalidateThisTokenItWillNukeTheComputerOfTheOwner' and the destructive commands 'rm -rf ~/' and 'rm -rf ~/Documents'. The honeytoken string is unique to this campaign with zero legitimate use; the rm-rf combined with a node/bun parent is the article's specific destructive-tripwire shape, distinguishing it from generic CI workspace cleanup.
ATT&CKT1485 T1491.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (FileName in~ ("rm","rm.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has "-rf"
          and (ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"\s~/?(\s|$)"
               or ProcessCommandLine has " $HOME"
               or ProcessCommandLine has "~/Documents"
               or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"\s/home/[^/\s]+/?(\s|$)"))
      or ProcessCommandLine has "IfYouInvalidateThisTokenItWillNukeTheComputerOfTheOwner"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","bun","sh","bash","dash","zsh","npm")
     or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("node","bun","npm","yarn","pnpm")
     or ProcessCommandLine has "IfYouInvalidateThisTokenItWillNukeTheComputerOfTheOwner"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, 
    InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
    InitiatingProcessParentCreationTime
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where (ActingProcessName endswith "rm" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "-rf"
          and (ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"\s~/?(\s|$)"
               or ActingProcessCommandLine has " $HOME"
               or ActingProcessCommandLine has "~/Documents"))
      or ActingProcessCommandLine has "IfYouInvalidateThisTokenItWillNukeTheComputerOfTheOwner"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node","bun","sh","bash","npm")
     or ActingProcessCommandLine has "IfYouInvalidateThisTokenItWillNukeTheComputerOfTheOwner"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Miasma Destructive Tripwire - rm -rf Home from Node or Bun
id: 6c8e3a17-9b42-4d51-a73c-1f9d5b8e7c4a
description: Detects 'rm -rf ~/' or honeytoken-triggered destructive deletions executed from a node/bun/npm process tree, signaling the Miasma fail-safe that wipes the maintainer's home directory when the planted honeytoken 'IfYouInvalidateThisTokenItWillNukeTheComputerOfTheOwner' is touched or revoked.
references:
  - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/02/preinstall-persistence-inside-red-hat-npm-miasma-credential-stealing-campaign/

  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:

      - '/sh'
      - '/bash'

  - CI workspace cleanup running 'rm -rf $HOME/work/*' (different target shape)
