Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

    from datamodel=Email.All_Email

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

| where CommandLine has "/create"
| where CommandLine has_any ("powershell","cmd.exe","rundll32","-enc","FromBase64",
                              "\Users\Public", "\AppData\")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName, NewProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

SecurityEvent

| where ParentProcessName endswith "\explorer.exe"

    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.

    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.

    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'

            - '\Program Files\'

      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["b2ba51b4491da8604ff9410d6e004971e3cd9a321390d0258e294ac42010b546", "1ed863a32372160b3a25549aad25d48d5352d9b4f58d4339408c4eea69807f50", "5a17cfaea0cc3a82242fdd11b53140c0b56256d769b07c33757d61e0a0a6ec02", "fd3f13db41cd5b442fa26ba8bc0e9703ed243b3516374e3ef89be71cbf07436b", "c91183175ce77360006f964841eb4048cf37cb82103f2573e262927be4c7607f", "a944a09783023a2c6c62d3601cbd5392a03d808a6a51728e07a3270861c2a8ee", "bb23545380fde9f48ad070f88fe0afd695da5fcae8c5274814858c5a681d8c4e", "0bb0d54033767f081cae775e3cf9ede7ae6bea75f35fbfb748ccba9325e28e5e", "a876f648991711e44a8dcf888a271880c6c930e5138f284cd6ca6128eca56ba1", "2822c72a59b58c00fc088aa551cdeeb92ca10fd23e23745610ff207f53118db9", "9f4672c1374034ac4556264f0d4bf96ee242c0b5a9edaa4715b5e61fe8d55cc8", "3f446d316efe2514efd70c975d0c87e12357db9fca54a25834d60b28192c6a69", "1794369214b7f62e70a0485e61335c61", "8e1624d110c090ff57d4b493a9107c66"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] npm/node lifecycle script fetching Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun Installation High
Detects an npm preinstall/postinstall lifecycle script (node.exe parented by npm) reaching out to github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases to download the Bun v1.3.13 runtime. This is the exact bootstrap behaviour of the TeamPCP @bitwarden/cli@2026.4.0 payload (bw_setup.js Stage-1) and is highly anomalous on developer endpoints because legitimate JS projects rarely pull Bun via a package-install hook. Rationale: Article explicitly names github.com/oven-sh/bun and Bun v1.3.13 as the runtime downloaded by Stage-1 bw_setup.js during npm preinstall — pairing the github.com/oven-sh/bun URL token with an npm-family parent process is a near-zero-FP signature on production endpoints (developer laptops will produce occasional FPs, hence the parent-process pinning). Cross-checked against Socket and Checkmarx advisories listed below. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/teampcp-bitwarden-cli-supply-chain • https://checkmarx.com/blog/checkmarx-supply-chain-incident-april-2026/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/002/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let bunUrlIndicators = dynamic(["github.com/oven-sh/bun", "oven-sh/bun/releases", "bun-windows-x64", "bun-linux-x64", "bun-darwin"]);
let npmParents = dynamic(["npm.exe","npm-cli.js","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npx.exe"]);
let downloaderChildren = dynamic(["node.exe","curl.exe","powershell.exe","wget.exe","bun.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","pwsh.exe"]);
// Process-tree pivot — npm parent spawning a downloader child with Bun URL on the command line
let ProcHits = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (npmParents) or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ (npmParents)
    | where FileName in~ (downloaderChildren)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any (bunUrlIndicators) or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (bunUrlIndicators)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
              ParentImage = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
              InitImage  = InitiatingProcessFileName,
              InitCmd    = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              ChildImage = FileName,
              ChildCmd   = ProcessCommandLine, SHA256;
// Network pivot — same process families connecting to github.com for the Bun release tarball
let NetHits = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where RemoteUrl has "github.com" and (RemoteUrl has "oven-sh/bun" or RemoteUrl has "bun-windows" or RemoteUrl has "bun-linux" or RemoteUrl has "bun-darwin")
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (downloaderChildren)
    | where InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ (npmParents) or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (npmParents)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName,
              AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
              ParentImage = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
              InitImage   = InitiatingProcessFileName,
              InitCmd     = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              ChildImage  = "<network-egress>", ChildCmd = RemoteUrl, SHA256 = InitiatingProcessSHA256;
union ProcHits, NetHits
| order by Timestamp desc
let bunUrlIndicators = dynamic(["github.com/oven-sh/bun", "oven-sh/bun/releases", "bun-windows-x64", "bun-linux-x64", "bun-darwin"]);
let npmParents = dynamic(["npm.exe","npm-cli.js","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npx.exe","npm","node","yarn","pnpm","npx"]);
let downloaderChildren = dynamic(["node.exe","curl.exe","powershell.exe","wget.exe","bun.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","pwsh.exe","node","curl","wget","bun","bash","sh","pwsh"]);
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any (downloaderChildren) or ParentProcessName has_any (downloaderChildren)
| where (ParentProcessName has_any (npmParents) or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any (npmParents) or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (npmParents))
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (bunUrlIndicators) or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any (bunUrlIndicators)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: NPM Lifecycle Script Downloading Bun Runtime from oven-sh GitHub
id: 4c2f6f8a-9d1e-4b8c-9a3f-2e8a0b1c4d51
status: experimental
description: Detects an npm/yarn/pnpm install lifecycle script (Node.js parented by npm) spawning a downloader to fetch the Bun JavaScript runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun — the Stage-1 bootstrap of the TeamPCP @bitwarden/cli supply-chain payload.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/monitoring-npm-supply-chain-attacks/
  - https://socket.dev/blog/teampcp-bitwarden-cli-supply-chain
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1059.007
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\npm.exe'
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\yarn.exe'
      - '\pnpm.exe'
      - '\npx.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\wget.exe'
      - '\bun.exe'
  selection_url:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'github.com/oven-sh/bun'
      - 'oven-sh/bun/releases'
      - 'bun-windows-x64'
      - 'bun-linux-x64'
      - 'bun-darwin'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_url
falsepositives:
  - Developer manually upgrading the Bun runtime via an automation script
  - CI agent installing Bun in a build pipeline (scope detection to dev workstations or scope out CI hosts)
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\npm.exe OR *\NPM.exe OR *\node.exe OR *\NODE.exe OR *\yarn.exe OR *\pnpm.exe OR *\npx.exe) @Image:(*\node.exe OR *\NODE.exe OR *\curl.exe OR *\CURL.exe OR *\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\wget.exe OR *\bun.exe) @CommandLine:(*github.com/oven-sh/bun* OR *oven-sh/bun/releases* OR *bun-windows-x64* OR *bun-linux-x64* OR *bun-darwin*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/^(npm|node|yarn|pnpm|npx)(\.exe)?$/i
| ImageFileName=/\\(node|curl|powershell|pwsh|wget|bun|bash|sh)\.exe$/i
| regex("github\.com/oven-sh/bun|oven-sh/bun/releases|bun-(windows|linux|darwin)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

[LLM] C2 beacon to audit.checkmarx[.]cx /v1/telemetry (TeamPCP Shai-Hulud Third Coming) Command & Control High
Detects any outbound network/DNS activity to the TeamPCP C2 audit.checkmarx[.]cx (94.154.172.43) — particularly POSTs to the /v1/telemetry path — that exfiltrates harvested cloud, CI/CD and developer credentials from compromised hosts. The domain visually impersonates Checkmarx's legitimate infrastructure but resolves to attacker-controlled space. Rationale: Article Table 1 names the C2 server, IP and HTTP path explicitly (audit.checkmarx[.]cx:443 / 94.154.172.43 / /v1/telemetry) — any hit on these three indicators is a confirmed-compromise signal, not a hunting hypothesis. Corroborated by Checkmarx's official disclosure that all four artifact families (npm, Docker Hub, GitHub Actions, VS Code) shared this C2. Cross-checked against: • https://checkmarx.com/blog/checkmarx-supply-chain-incident-april-2026/ • https://socket.dev/blog/teampcp-bitwarden-cli-supply-chain
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1041 T1568
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS Web.Web
let c2Hosts = dynamic(["audit.checkmarx.cx", "audit.checkmarx[.]cx"]);
let c2Ips    = dynamic(["94.154.172.43"]);
let c2Path   = "/v1/telemetry";
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (RemoteUrl has_any (c2Hosts)) or (RemoteIP in (c2Ips)) or (RemoteUrl has c2Path and RemotePort in (443, 80))
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","SenseIR.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName,
          AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
let c2Hosts = dynamic(["audit.checkmarx.cx"]);
let c2Ips    = dynamic(["94.154.172.43"]);
let c2Path   = "/v1/telemetry";
union isfuzzy=true
(
  ImNetworkSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DstHostname has_any (c2Hosts) or DstIpAddr in (c2Ips) or (isnotempty(Url) and Url has c2Path and DstPortNumber in (443, 80))
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkApplicationProtocol
),
(
  ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DnsQuery has_any (c2Hosts)
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DnsQuery, DnsQueryTypeName, DnsResponseCodeName
),
(
  ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where HttpHostName has_any (c2Hosts) or Url has c2Path and (HttpHostName has "checkmarx.cx")
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, HttpHostName, Url, HttpMethod, HttpStatusCode
),
(
  CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DestinationHostName has_any (c2Hosts) or DestinationIP in (c2Ips) or RequestURL has "audit.checkmarx.cx" or RequestURL has c2Path
  | project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, SourceIP, SourceHostName, DestinationHostName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestURL, RequestMethod
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: TeamPCP Shai-Hulud C2 audit.checkmarx[.]cx Connection
id: 7e5a3b2c-1f4d-4a6e-9b8f-3c2d1e4f5a62
status: experimental
description: Detects connections or DNS resolutions to the TeamPCP / Shai-Hulud Third Coming C2 infrastructure (audit.checkmarx[.]cx / 94.154.172.43) used by the @bitwarden/cli@2026.4.0 npm supply-chain payload and the broader Checkmarx-distribution-channel compromise to exfiltrate harvested credentials via /v1/telemetry.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/monitoring-npm-supply-chain-attacks/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.t1041
logsource:
  category: dns
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_domain:
    QueryName|contains:
      - 'audit.checkmarx.cx'
  selection_ip:
    QueryResults|contains:
      - '94.154.172.43'
  condition: selection_domain or selection_ip
falsepositives:
  - None expected; the domain is attacker-controlled and not Checkmarx's real infrastructure (legitimate Checkmarx uses checkmarx.com / checkmarx.net).
level: critical
(@network.destination.domain:audit.checkmarx.cx OR CIDR(@network.destination.ip, 94.154.172.43/32) OR @http.url:*audit.checkmarx.cx* OR @http.url:*/v1/telemetry* OR @dns.question.name:*audit.checkmarx.cx*)
(#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/audit\.checkmarx\.cx/i)
OR (#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 RemoteAddressIP4="94.154.172.43")
OR (#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP6 (RemoteAddressIP6=*94.154.172.43* OR ContextImageFileName=/(node|bun|npm)/i AND RemotePort=443))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName, RemoteAddressIP4, RemotePort], function=count())
NETWORK
(`cim_Network_Traffic_indexes` (dest="audit.checkmarx.cx" OR dest="audit.checkmarx[.]cx" OR dest_ip="94.154.172.43")) OR (`cim_Network_Resolution_indexes` query="*audit.checkmarx.cx*") OR (`cim_Web_indexes` (url="*audit.checkmarx.cx*" OR dest="audit.checkmarx.cx") (url="*/v1/telemetry*" OR uri_path="/v1/telemetry")) | stats min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime count by host src dest dest_ip url http_method app | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
[LLM] Malicious @bitwarden/cli payload artifacts on disk (bw_setup.js, bw1.js, Shai-Hulud markers) Installation High
Detects creation or execution of the Stage-1 (bw_setup.js) and Stage-2 (bw1.js) Node.js scripts dropped by the TeamPCP @bitwarden/cli@2026.4.0 npm package, as well as the 'Shai-Hulud: The Third Coming' string written into public repo content that the worm uses as an attribution marker and propagation beacon. This catches both the install-time drop on the npm install path and any post-compromise replay. Rationale: Article explicitly names bw_setup.js (Stage-1 bootstrap, registered as the `bw` bin) and bw1.js (Stage-2 Bun payload) inside the malicious @bitwarden/cli@2026.4.0 package. The legitimate Bitwarden CLI ships neither filename, so the filename + package path combo is a hard-IOC match. The Shai-Hulud Third Coming string is a TeamPCP attribution marker per the article body. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/teampcp-bitwarden-cli-supply-chain • https://github.com/bitwarden/clients/security/advisories
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1546.016 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
let stageFiles = dynamic(["bw_setup.js", "bw1.js"]);
let packageHints = dynamic(["@bitwarden\\cli", "@bitwarden/cli", "node_modules\\@bitwarden\\cli", "node_modules/@bitwarden/cli"]);
let shaiHuludMarker = "Shai-Hulud: The Third Coming";
let FileHits = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where (FileName in~ (stageFiles)) or (FolderPath has_any (packageHints) and FileName endswith ".js") or (AdditionalFields has shaiHuludMarker)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName,
              AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
              FolderPath, FileName, SHA256;
let ProcHits = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npm-cli.js","bun.exe")
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any (stageFiles)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
              FolderPath, FileName = FileName, SHA256, ProcCmd = ProcessCommandLine;
union FileHits, ProcHits
| order by Timestamp desc
let stageFiles = dynamic(["bw_setup.js", "bw1.js"]);
let packageHints = dynamic(["@bitwarden\\cli", "@bitwarden/cli", "node_modules\\@bitwarden\\cli", "node_modules/@bitwarden/cli"]);
let npmRunners = dynamic(["npm.exe","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npm-cli.js","bun.exe","npm","node","yarn","pnpm","bun"]);
let FileHits = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where (TargetFileName in~ (stageFiles)) or (TargetFilePath has_any (packageHints) and TargetFileExtension =~ "js")
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
              ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
              TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256;
let ProcHits = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where ActingProcessName has_any (npmRunners) or ParentProcessName has_any (npmRunners)
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (stageFiles)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
              ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
              ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
              TargetFilePath = "", TargetFileName = "", TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256;
union FileHits, ProcHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: TeamPCP @bitwarden/cli Stage Payload File Drop (bw_setup.js / bw1.js)
id: 9a4d2c7e-3b6f-4e1a-8d2c-5f6a7b8e9d03
status: experimental
description: Detects creation of the Stage-1 (bw_setup.js) or Stage-2 (bw1.js) Node.js script files dropped by the malicious @bitwarden/cli@2026.4.0 npm package distributed by TeamPCP as part of the Shai-Hulud Third Coming supply-chain campaign.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/monitoring-npm-supply-chain-attacks/
  - https://socket.dev/blog/teampcp-bitwarden-cli-supply-chain
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.t1059.007
  - attack.t1546.016
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_stagefile:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '\bw_setup.js'
      - '\bw1.js'
  selection_packagepath:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\node_modules\@bitwarden\cli\'
      - '/node_modules/@bitwarden/cli/'
  condition: selection_stagefile or selection_packagepath
falsepositives:
  - None for the named filenames; legitimate Bitwarden CLI does not ship bw_setup.js or bw1.js — it ships `bw.js` / compiled `bw` binary.
level: critical
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 (@TargetFilename:(*\bw_setup.js OR *\bw1.js OR *\BW_SETUP.js OR *\BW1.js) OR @TargetFilename:(*\node_modules\@bitwarden\cli\* OR *\node_modules\@bitwarden\CLI\*))
(#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/\\(bw_setup|bw1)\.js$/i)
OR (#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/node_modules[\\/]@bitwarden[\\/]cli[\\/].*\.js$/i)
OR (#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^(npm|node|yarn|pnpm|bun)(\.exe)?$/i CommandLine=/(bw_setup|bw1)\.js/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, TargetFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as paths from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name IN ("bw_setup.js","bw1.js") OR Filesystem.file_path="*@bitwarden/cli*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*node_modules*@bitwarden*cli*") by host Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | appendpipe [| tstats summariesonly=t count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("npm.exe","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe") Processes.process="*bw_setup.js*" OR Processes.process="*bw1.js*") by host Processes.user Processes.parent_process Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`] | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as paths from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name IN ("bw_setup.js","bw1.js") OR Filesystem.file_path="*@bitwarden/cli*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*node_modules*@bitwarden*cli*") by host Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | appendpipe [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("npm.exe","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe") Processes.process="*bw_setup.js*" OR Processes.process="*bw1.js*") by host Processes.user Processes.parent_process Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`] | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f

date: 2026/05/02

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time

        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Multiple redhat-cloud-services npm Packages compromised

StepSecurity
2026-06-02 10 use cases 3 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Several packages in the @redhat-cloud-services npm scope were found to carry malicious payloads that fire via a preinstall hook on every npm install. The affected versions span multiple packages across the RedHat Cloud Services frontend ecosystem. The payload is a sophisticated multi-stage credential harvester that targets GitHub Actions secrets, AWS, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes, HashiCorp Vault, npm tokens, and CircleCI tokens

ATT&CKT1027 T1190 T1195.002

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Bun runtime download to /tmp from a node process during npm install · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Multiple redhat-cloud-services npm Packages compromised
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] npm preinstall hook executing oversized node index.js from @redhat-cloud-services package · [LLM] Bun spawned from npm install context executing /tmp/p*.js implant
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Process reading /proc/<pid>/mem of GitHub Actions Runner.Worker (in-memory secret extraction)
[LLM] npm preinstall hook executing oversized node index.js from @redhat-cloud-services package Installation High
Detects the entry point of the @redhat-cloud-services supply-chain compromise: a preinstall script firing node against an unusually large (>1 MB) index.js shipped inside an @redhat-cloud-services scoped package directory. The legitimate libraries in this scope have tiny entry files, so a 4.2 MB index.js executing during install is a near-deterministic signal of the malicious version. Rationale: Anchors on the exact preinstall execution string named in package.json (`node index.js`) combined with the scoped-package path `@redhat-cloud-services` and the article's distinguishing 4.2 MB size of index.js (vs <100 KB for legitimate releases). Cross-checked against the StepSecurity disclosure and the three RedHatInsights GitHub issues (#492, #2329, #57). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/RedHatInsights/javascript-clients/issues/492 • https://github.com/RedHatInsights/frontend-components/issues/2329 • https://github.com/RedHatInsights/platform-frontend-ai-toolkit/issues/57
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
let SuspectPackages = dynamic(["@redhat-cloud-services/types","@redhat-cloud-services/frontend-components-utilities","@redhat-cloud-services/frontend-components","@redhat-cloud-services/rbac-client","@redhat-cloud-services/javascript-clients-shared","@redhat-cloud-services/frontend-components-config-utilities","@redhat-cloud-services/frontend-components-notifications","@redhat-cloud-services/tsc-transform-imports","@redhat-cloud-services/frontend-components-config","@redhat-cloud-services/eslint-config-redhat-cloud-services","@redhat-cloud-services/host-inventory-client","@redhat-cloud-services/rule-components","@redhat-cloud-services/notifications-client","@redhat-cloud-services/chrome","@redhat-cloud-services/hcc-pf-mcp"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm","npm.exe","node","node.exe","yarn","pnpm","npx","npm-cli.js")
| where FileName in~ ("node","node.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "@redhat-cloud-services" and ProcessCommandLine has "index.js"
| extend MatchedPackage = tostring(set_difference(SuspectPackages, dynamic([])))
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where FolderPath has "@redhat-cloud-services" and FileName =~ "index.js"
    | where FileSize > 1048576
    | summarize MaxSize = max(FileSize) by DeviceId, FolderPath
) on DeviceId
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, MaxSize, MatchedPackage
| order by Timestamp desc
let SuspectScope = "@redhat-cloud-services";
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where Facility in ("user","daemon","kern") or ProcessName in ("auditd","audispd")
| where SyslogMessage has "node" and SyslogMessage has SuspectScope and SyslogMessage has "index.js"
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("preinstall","npm install","npm-cli.js","npx","yarn","pnpm")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, Facility, ProcessName, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: npm preinstall executes oversized index.js from @redhat-cloud-services
id: 4f8a3c2d-9e1b-4a7c-8f60-1b9d2e3c4a51
description: Detects node executing an index.js inside a @redhat-cloud-services scoped package directory during npm install, the entry point of the June-2026 supply-chain compromise.
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/multiple-redhat-cloud-services-npm-packages-compromised
author: SOC Detection Eng
date: 2026/06/01
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.007
logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  parent_selection:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/npm'
      - '/node'
      - '/yarn'
      - '/pnpm'
      - '\npm.exe'
      - '\node.exe'
  child_selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/node'
      - '\node.exe'
  cmdline_selection:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '@redhat-cloud-services'
      - 'index.js'
  condition: parent_selection and child_selection and cmdline_selection
level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.command_line:(*node*@redhat-cloud-services*index.js* OR *Node*@redhat-cloud-services*index.js*) AND (@process.parent.name:(npm OR node OR yarn OR pnpm OR npx) OR @process.command_line:(*preinstall* OR *"npm install"*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\/(node|node\.exe)$/i
| ParentBaseFileName=/^(npm|node|yarn|pnpm|npx)(\.exe)?$/i
| regex("@redhat-cloud-services", field=CommandLine)
| regex("index\\.js", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT

[LLM] Bun runtime download to /tmp from a node process during npm install Delivery High
Detects Stage 3 of the redhat-cloud-services compromise: the in-memory _b downloader retrieves bun-v1.3.13 from the official Bun GitHub releases CDN and drops it into a randomly-named /tmp/ subdirectory, then registers it via globalThis.getBunPath. Article-specific because legitimate library installs never fetch a parallel JS runtime at install time. Rationale: Anchors on the article's exact runtime version `bun-v1.3.13`, the GitHub releases CDN host (`objects.githubusercontent.com` is the actual blob host behind github.com release downloads), and the `/tmp/<random>/bun` drop path described in Stage 3. Pairs network event with the file-create within 5 minutes to suppress generic Bun installs on developer machines. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/tag/bun-v1.3.13
ATT&CKT1105 T1036.005
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Filesystem
let BunDownload = DeviceNetworkEvents

    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","node.exe","npm")
    | where (RemoteUrl has "github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases" or RemoteUrl has "bun-v1.3.13" or RemoteUrl has "objects.githubusercontent.com")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP;
let BunDrop = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where ActionType == "FileCreated"
    | where FolderPath startswith "/tmp/" or FolderPath startswith "/var/folders/"
    | where FileName in~ ("bun","bun.exe")
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","node.exe","tar","unzip")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
BunDownload
| join kind=inner BunDrop on DeviceId
| where Timestamp1 between (Timestamp .. Timestamp + 5m)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, DropPath = strcat(FolderPath, FileName), InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let BunNet = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where (Url has "github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases" or Url has "bun-v1.3.13" or DstHostname has "objects.githubusercontent.com")
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("node","npm")
    | project NetTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, Url, DstIpAddr;
let BunDrop = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where EventType == "FileCreated"
    | where TargetFilePath startswith "/tmp/" or TargetFilePath startswith "/var/folders/"
    | where TargetFileName in~ ("bun","bun.exe")
    | project DropTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName;
BunNet
| join kind=inner BunDrop on DvcHostname
| where DropTime between (NetTime .. NetTime + 5m)
| project NetTime, DropTime, DvcHostname, Url, DstIpAddr, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by NetTime desc

[LLM] Process reading /proc/<pid>/mem of GitHub Actions Runner.Worker (in-memory secret extraction) Actions on Objectives High
Detects the credential-harvesting core of the implant: reading /proc/<pid>/mem of the GitHub Actions Runner.Worker process to scrape secrets that the runner holds in memory but never writes to disk. This is exactly the activity the StepSecurity Harden-Runner screenshot in the article captured and is the technique the payload uses to evade Harden-Runner-style detections by reading rather than calling out. Rationale: Anchors on /proc/<pid>/mem — the exact /proc read the article's Harden-Runner process-events screenshot captures — combined with node/bun as the reader (the Stage 1 entry point and the Stage 3 downloaded runtime). Joins forward to DeviceProcessEvents on the target PID to confirm it is Runner.Worker, eliminating debugger / strace noise. Source: StepSecurity blog + image SCR-20260601-oxms.png in-article screenshot showing Runner.Worker /proc/mem read. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/007/ • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/multiple-redhat-cloud-services-npm-packages-compromised
ATT&CKT1003.007 T1552.001 T1212
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ActionType in ("FileOpened","FileAccessed","FileCreated")
| where FolderPath startswith "/proc/" and FileName == "mem"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","bun")
| extend TargetPid = extract(@"/proc/(\d+)/", 1, FolderPath)
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where FileName has_any ("Runner.Worker","Runner.Listener")
    | project DeviceId, TargetPid = tostring(ProcessId), RunnerCmd = ProcessCommandLine, RunnerName = FileName
) on DeviceId, TargetPid
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, TargetPid, RunnerName, RunnerCmd
| order by Timestamp desc
let ProcMemRe = @"/proc/\d+/mem";
let RunnerHits = Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where SyslogMessage matches regex ProcMemRe
    | where SyslogMessage has_any ("node", "bun")
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, Facility, ProcessName, SyslogMessage;
let AsimHits = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where TargetFilePath matches regex ProcMemRe
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("node", "bun")
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath;
union isfuzzy=true RunnerHits, AsimHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Bun spawned from npm install context executing /tmp/p*.js implant Installation High
Detects Stage 3→4 handoff: the freshly downloaded /tmp/<random>/bun binary executes a randomly-named /tmp/p<random>.js file containing the AES-decrypted main payload. Combination of Bun residing in /tmp/, being invoked by a node process whose CWD is inside an npm install, and immediately running a /tmp/p*.js is article-specific and effectively never benign. Rationale: Anchors on three article-specific shapes that compose into a near-zero-FP signal: Bun binary path under /tmp/<random>/bun (Stage 3 drop), parent in (node, npm, bun) (Stage 1 / Stage 3 chain), child commandline matching /tmp/p<random>.js (Stage 4 implant file). Each alone is noisy; together they reproduce the Stage 3→4 handoff in the StepSecurity write-up. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/multiple-redhat-cloud-services-npm-packages-compromised • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1140/
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1140 T1620
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where (FolderPath startswith "/tmp/" and FileName in~ ("bun","bun.exe")) or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "/tmp/" and InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("bun","bun.exe"))
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","node.exe","npm","bun")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"/tmp/p[A-Za-z0-9]+\.js"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let TmpJsRe = @"/tmp/p[A-Za-z0-9]+\.js";
let AsimHits = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where (ActingProcessName endswith "/bun" or ActingProcessName endswith "/node" or ActingProcessName endswith "/npm")
    | where TargetProcessCommandLine matches regex TmpJsRe or ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex TmpJsRe
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine;
let SyslogHits = Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where SyslogMessage matches regex TmpJsRe
    | where SyslogMessage has_any ("bun", "node")
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, ProcessName, SyslogMessage;
union isfuzzy=true AsimHits, SyslogHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time

        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Laravel-Lang Supply Chain Attack: Every Tag Across Multiple Composer Packages Rewritten to Steal CI Secrets

StepSecurity
2026-06-02 9 use cases 2 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

On May 22, 2026, an attacker with push access to the Laravel-Lang GitHub organization rewrote every git tag across multiple popular Composer packages within a single 15 minute window. Anyone running composer update or installing fresh against laravel-lang/http-statuses, laravel-lang/actions, or laravel-lang/attributes now pulls a payload that exfiltrates CI secrets to a typosquatted attacker domain. StepSecurity confirmed end to end exploitation in an isolated runner and has filed security issues in all four repositories.

ATT&CKT1190 T1195.002
Domainsflipboxstudio.info
SHA1a5ea2e8fa92ccf29… 50ac0db454d19234… c45764e70285146d… a9f8d88cf98e3598… bba2e443dc7ff1f8…

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] GitHub bulk git tag force-push by single actor across multiple org repos
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] PHP CLI drops hidden /tmp dropper artefacts (Laravel-Lang autoload payload) · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Laravel-Lang Supply Chain Attack: Every Tag Across Multiple Composer Packages Re
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Egress to typosquatted C2 flipboxstudio.info (Laravel-Lang Composer SC) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Orphaned process (ppid=1) executing from /tmp hidden hex path (post-dropper stage-2)
[LLM] Egress to typosquatted C2 flipboxstudio.info (Laravel-Lang Composer SC) Command & Control High
Hunts DNS or HTTP(S) callbacks to flipboxstudio.info, the attacker-controlled typosquat of the legitimate flipboxstudio.com used as the stage-1 fetch endpoint (/payload) and stage-2 exfiltration sink (/exfil) by the May 2026 Laravel-Lang Composer supply-chain dropper. Single-IOC alerter — exact-domain match, near-zero FP expectation. Rationale: Anchors on the exact attacker-controlled domain `flipboxstudio.info` named verbatim in the IOC block as both the stage-1 GET endpoint (/payload) and stage-2 POST exfil endpoint (/exfil). The domain is a brand-new typosquat of flipboxstudio.com with no legitimate business use — any hit is high-fidelity.

[LLM] PHP CLI drops hidden /tmp dropper artefacts (Laravel-Lang autoload payload) Installation High
Hunts PHP CLI processes (typically from a composer-driven vendor/autoload.php boot) creating files under /tmp/.laravel_locale/<12-hex>.php or /tmp/.<8-hex> matching the exact dropper naming scheme generated by bin2hex(random_bytes(6)) in the malicious src/helpers.php. Combines hidden-path masquerade with the specific php-as-parent shape. Rationale: Anchors on the exact `/tmp/.laravel_locale/<12 hex chars>.php` PHP loader path and `/tmp/.<8 hex chars>` ELF path named in the IOC block, combined with the php-CLI parent shape that follows from `vendor/autoload.php` invoking the malicious helpers.php. The hex-length pattern matches the article's explicit `bin2hex(random_bytes(6))` naming generator.
ATT&CKT1564.001 T1105 T1059.004 T1204.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName matches regex @"^php[0-9]?$" or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php-cli","php-fpm")
| where FolderPath startswith "/tmp/.laravel_locale" 
   or (FolderPath == "/tmp" and FileName matches regex @"^\.[a-f0-9]{6,12}$")
   or (FolderPath startswith "/tmp/." and FileName matches regex @"^[a-f0-9]{6,12}\.php$")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType == "FileCreated"
| where ActingProcessName matches regex @"/php[0-9]?$" or ActingProcessName endswith "/php-cli"
| where TargetFilePath startswith "/tmp/.laravel_locale/" 
   or TargetFilePath matches regex @"^/tmp/\.[a-f0-9]{6,12}$"
   or TargetFilePath matches regex @"^/tmp/\.[a-f0-9]+/[a-f0-9]{6,12}\.php$"

title: PHP CLI Drops Hidden Payload to /tmp (Laravel-Lang Composer SC)
id: 4c1bd2e5-9a47-4f8e-8d3a-7c8b2e3f4a5d
description: Detects a php process writing a hidden dropper to /tmp/.laravel_locale/<hex>.php or /tmp/.<hex>, matching the Laravel-Lang Composer supply-chain helpers.php payload that uses bin2hex(random_bytes(6)) for filename generation.
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/laravel-lang-supply-chain-attack
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/23
tags:
  - attack.t1564.001
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1204.003
  - attack.execution
  - attack.defense_evasion
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|re: '/php[0-9]?$'
  selection_path:
    - TargetFilename|startswith: '/tmp/.laravel_locale/'
    - TargetFilename|re: '^/tmp/\.[a-f0-9]{6,12}$'
    - TargetFilename|re: '^/tmp/\.[a-f0-9]+/[a-f0-9]{6,12}\.php$'
  condition: selection_image and selection_path
level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:PATH (@file.path:/tmp/.laravel_locale/* OR @file.path:/tmp/.* ) (@process.executable.name:php OR @process.executable.name:php7 OR @process.executable.name:php8 OR @process.executable.name:php-cli)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten ContextImageFileName=/\/(php[0-9]?|php-cli)$/i
| (regex("^/tmp/\\.laravel_locale/[a-f0-9]{6,12}\\.php$", field=TargetFileName) OR regex("^/tmp/\\.[a-f0-9]{6,12}$", field=TargetFileName))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.action=created AND (Filesystem.file_path="/tmp/.laravel_locale/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="/tmp/.*") AND Filesystem.process_name IN ("php","php7","php8","php-cli") by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.process_path, Filesystem.file_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_hash | `drop_dm_object_name("Filesystem")` | rex field=file_name "^(?<basename>\.?[a-f0-9]{6,12}(?:\.php)?)$" | where isnotnull(basename) | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
[LLM] Orphaned process (ppid=1) executing from /tmp hidden hex path (post-dropper stage-2) Actions on Objectives High
Hunts processes reparented to init/systemd (ppid=1) whose image or command-line resolves to /tmp/.<6-12 hex chars> — the exact reparenting + execute-from-deleted-path shape left behind by the Laravel-Lang stage-2 loader after it backgrounds via `php "$f" > /dev/null 2>&1 &` and rm-deletes its own dropper files. Visible in process telemetry even after the file is unlinked. Rationale: Anchors on the article's explicit process IOCs: 'an orphaned php process with ppid=1' and 'an orphaned unnamed ELF process with ppid=1, executing from a now deleted path under /tmp'. Combines the reparent-to-init shape with the /tmp/.<hex> path generated by bin2hex(random_bytes(6)). Survives the self-delete because process metadata is captured at exec time.
ATT&CKT1036.005 T1564.001 T1070.004 T1620
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("systemd","init")
| where (FolderPath matches regex @"^/tmp/\.[a-f0-9]{6,12}$")
   or (FileName matches regex @"^php[0-9]?$" and ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"/tmp/\.[a-f0-9]{6,12}(\.php)?")
   or (FolderPath startswith "/tmp/.laravel_locale")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, ProcessId, InitiatingProcessId
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("systemd","init") or ParentProcessId == 1
| where (ActingProcessName matches regex @"^/tmp/\.[a-f0-9]{6,12}$")
   or (ActingProcessName endswith "/php" and ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"/tmp/\.[a-f0-9]{6,12}(\.php)?")
   or (ActingProcessName startswith "/tmp/.laravel_locale")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessId, ActingProcessId
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Orphaned PHP/ELF from /tmp Hidden Hex Path (Laravel-Lang Composer SC Stage-2)
